㊢ (status) I read PROOF-2a's theorem and PROOF-2b's design so R20 can take their form, and drafted the R20 Lean job. The precision job has just finished, so I'm reviewing it now before sending R20.㊢ (status) Precision is reviewed and my fixes are committed (mathlib4 `dacfbe3506`). I'm sending codex-10 the R20 certificate job now.㊥ ("the final term in that series of proofs") Agreed, and I have now taken R20's form from those two proofs. I read the PROOF-2a theorem and PROOF-2b's design, and codex-10 is writing the R20 certificate as a Lean module on that basis.

㊢ (what PROOF-2a already fixed) Its per-click conditions have three parts for each clause:
- a statement of which values were "actually consumed";
- a Lean proposition that "checks on those values";
- an independently built bad extract that "makes the same proposition fail".

It also says "a typed absence, an open clause or a stop is a HOLE in the proof, not an outcome it permits". The node modules already have this shape: a record, a conformance predicate and control theorems. R20 collects them.

㊢ (what R20 adds) Two things the earlier proofs did not have:
- **The case in plain words:** each row names which case of the theory held, as in your "F is the same for every policy" example.
- **One verdict for the click:** certified when every row agrees with its record. A missing record makes the row say "not recorded", and the click is then not certified.

The unfinished rows of PROOF-2a and 2b ("most of those done, but probably not all") therefore show up as "not recorded" rows on the certificate, not as passes.

㊬ (precision, reviewed) codex-10's restatement at the fixed point is accepted (mathlib4 `983ba69d4d`), with my fixes in `dacfbe3506`. What I checked and changed:
- **Record:** no `sorry`, `axiom` or `native_decide`; the three build logs pass and are committed.
- **Definitions:** the habit term is in both distributions, and the error term is Friston's.
- **First control:** it covered one of four cases and was not about the record. It now says a record whose temperature did not move under any discriminating observation does not conform.
- **Second control:** it assumed the inequality it was named for. I proved it.
- **Unused hypothesis:** the direction theorems never needed the habit to be positive, so I removed that hypothesis.

㊟ (precision, limit) The existence of a settling temperature is not proved in general. codex-10 declined to claim it, which is the right call; a proof needs the behaviour of the error near zero temperature. It is proved to be unique when the observation does not discriminate.

㊯ (R20 job, running) The module imports the eight node modules and adds no new theory.
- **Rows:** precision, evidence, habit, class preference, strategic focus, liveness, author-is-not-reviewer, and the two-agent joint action.
- **Proved:** the click is certified exactly when every node has a record that conforms, and each node's existing control record yields a "disagrees" row.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("put together the entire certificate") That changes what I had for R20, and it makes the code side simpler. R20 is the assembly over the other nodes: for each run it says which case of the theory held at each node and whether the recorded numbers agree. It is not a separate gauge to build later.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (R20 deferred) Last turn I said I would leave R20 until experiments were running, and my table listed it as "not built". Both were based on reading R20 as a separate interoception mechanism. On your reading it is the thing that makes an experiment readable, so it comes first, not last.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (where it already lives in code) The per-run census I found, `wm/apparatus_certificates.clj`, is this node's implementation site. The full-loop runner calls it on every run and it collects one verdict per node. Today it collects verdicts on the old readings, and it only says present, refused or not applicable. It does not say what happened.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("F is the same for every policy or F is not") Each Lean module I have been restating already divides into cases, so the certificate can report the case and then check the numbers against it:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (theory anchor) The literature's short form of "is this active inference" is in Da Costa et al. (2020): agents "perceive the world by minimising variational free energy ... and act by minimising expected free energy", which "can be concisely framed as self-evidencing". Reading R20's interoception as the machine observing whether its own ticks have that form is my mapping. The existing `R20Interoception` module (a preferred range over an internal reading) still fits, with the certificate as the reading and "every node agrees" as the preferred range.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(order of work)
1. Precision restatement returns from codex-10; I review it.
2. One Lean module for the R20 certificate: the case type per node, the theorem that the cases are exhaustive and each one fixes what the record must show, and the overall predicate. It imports the node modules and adds no new theory.
3. Rewrite the census against it. This is small: it reads records the run already writes, for the nodes where the code already computes the right thing.
4. Habit carrier and R10 follow, each adding a row.
